driver_summary.description: One short paragraph telling the driver what to do differently in this car, and why. It is the only free text the preflight overlay shows, so it must say something the Fit and Use rows do not already state: "this is a dog box" is already carried by the gearbox type, while "rev-match every downshift or the dogs will not engage" is the reason to read it. Optional. When absent the overlay shows no note panel at all rather than padding the card with restatement. Every claim in it must be supported by the record's own curated values or its cited sources.

archetypeClassification.description: Which control archetype this record's transmission matches, declared by a reviewer and never derived by tooling. Optional: a record without it is unreviewed for archetype, which is different from one reviewed and found to match none. The archetype supplies no values - authentic_controls.transmission stays the authoritative, fully written-out description of the car - so this block can only ever describe the record, never change it. It is a curation and review aid and carries no evidence: it must never appear in a provenance claim or a source reference. See docs/archetypes.md.

archetype_id.description: The archetype in data/v1/archetypes.json. Required when classification is matches or deviates, and must be absent otherwise.

classification.description: matches - every field equals the archetype. deviates - the record departs from it in the declared ways, and nowhere else. no-archetype - reviewed, and this mechanism genuinely matches none. undetermined - cannot be classified yet, because an unknown sits in a field that separates two or more archetypes. The last two mirror the no/unknown distinction the rest of the dataset draws: one is a conclusion, the other is a gap, and collapsing them would lose the reason to drive the car again.

deviations.description: Every field where the record departs from its archetype, each declared with a reason. Required and non-empty when classification is deviates, and empty or absent otherwise. A departure the record does not declare is a validation failure, which is what keeps an unintended change loud rather than letting it pass as one more record that happens to differ.

path.description: JSON Pointer to the departing field, inside this record's transmission block.

basis.description: Why this car departs. The departure is usually the research finding, so this line is the one a reviewer reads first.

Why this classification was reached. Required when classification is no-archetype or undetermined, where nothing else records the reviewer's reasoning. For undetermined, name the field whose unknown blocks the decision: that is what a future drive has to settle.

additional_classes.description: Further real-world categories the same car competes in, where one car carries more than one category name: a Porsche 963 is GTP in IMSA and Hypercar in the WEC. `class` stays the primary category so existing consumers keep working.

first_gear_position.description: Where first gear sits in the gate. A dogleg pattern only states that first is outside the racing plane; it does not establish which side, and at least one car mirrors it.

shape.description: Rim shape, decided by the rim itself; the car's racing class never enters into it. Take the first that matches: gt-formula (molded grips at about 9 and 3 with a control face between them, so the hands stay put - the rim modern GT, formula and prototype cars all share, usually carrying a display and rev lights), yoke (two grips with nothing joining them over the top), d-shaped (a conventional rim you can grip anywhere, flattened at the bottom, the top, or both), round (a conventional continuous circle). Use other when none match and unknown when the rim was not seen. gt-style, formula and prototype are deprecated: they split one rim three ways by racing class, produced the same client icon, and asked reviewers for a judgment that changed no advice. They stay in the enum so existing records remain valid, but must not be used for new records.

integrated_display.description: Whether the rim itself carries a readout: a graphical LCD, an LED numeric gear indicator, or a segment display all count. A dash mounted on the car rather than the rim does not, and shift lights alone do not.

shift_lights.description: Whether the rim carries shift or rev lights, recorded independently of integrated_display.

open_top.description: Whether rim material joins the grips over the top of the rim. It asks about material, not about where the rim is held, and it describes the rim rather than deciding its shape: a gt-formula rim may be either, a yoke is always yes, and a d-shaped or round rim is no.

aeroPackage.description: An aero configuration a simulator selects from the circuit rather than from the driver. The vocabulary is closed: these are the only packages any curated simulator applies, and a name-shaped identity carries at most one of them.

value.description: The exact string the simulator reports. Where aero_packages is present this is the base name with no package suffix, and the suffixed forms are derived from it; everywhere else it is the whole identity, written out.

aero_packages.description:
The aero configurations this identity covers, expanded into one exact lookup key each when the database is loaded. It replaces writing every suffixed spelling by hand: 164 of 404 curated telemetry names were a base name plus one of four suffixes, and 42 of those were never observed at all but derived by a reviewer and marked as such.

This is not fuzzy matching and does not relax exact matching. Expansion produces exact strings and nothing is rewritten at match time, so an identity a record does not declare still fails to match, still logs as unmatched, and still shows the driver a blank card rather than another car's answer. The failure mode stays what it is today.

How a package renders is a property of the simulator, not of the record: AMS2 appends ' - High Downforce' and its siblings to the base name, and renders `base` as the bare name. A simulator that names its variants unsystematically declares nothing here and writes its identities out literally, exactly as every record does today.

Only a telemetry-name may carry this, and the packages a car offers differ by class and must be read per class rather than assumed from another car: two of the AMS2 open-wheel classes offer no low-downforce package at all.
